data.content_ref: inline:The Pragmatic Wager (SRC_005) depends on the Asymmetry of Risk (SRC_019) as its structural mechanism: the wager is rational only if the cost of rejecting a well-corroborated theory (potential loss of truth) strictly exceeds the cost of accepting a falsified one. This relation is refuted if it can be shown that the 'asymmetry' is merely a restatement of inductive expectation (that the future will resemble the past) rather than a distinct logical feature of falsification, thereby collapsing the wager into the induction it seeks to avoid.
